scope: SolidStart v2 with Solid v1, Solid Router v1 and Vite v8. Subpath and HTTP error findings also inspect source revision 68ce20b; deployment plugins are named separately.

ssr.note: renderToString produces synchronous HTML and hydration metadata.

streaming.note: renderToStream integrates Suspense fallback boundaries and streams their resolved content; the host must preserve flushing.

suspense.note: renderToStream integrates Suspense fallback boundaries and streams their resolved content; the host must preserve flushing.

client.note: hydrate attaches reactive behavior to SSR HTML; render creates a client application root.

ssg.note: The documented Nitro plugin prerenders listed or crawled routes into static output. Server functions still require a server.
ssg.label: Nitro prerendering

csr.note: hydrate attaches reactive behavior to SSR HTML; render creates a client application root.

serverOnly.note: The reviewed API excludes server modules or function bodies from browser builds, but does not establish server-only UI components whose implementation is omitted from hydration bundles. These are different capabilities.
serverOnly.label: Server modules / functions only

partialRendering.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart rendering guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

routing.note: FileRoutes maps page files and dynamic segments; Solid Router supplies nested layout/navigation behavior. SolidStart v2 also supports a TanStack Router integration.

layouts.note: FileRoutes maps page files and dynamic segments; Solid Router supplies nested layout/navigation behavior. SolidStart v2 also supports a TanStack Router integration.

dynamicRoutes.note: FileRoutes maps page files and dynamic segments; Solid Router supplies nested layout/navigation behavior. SolidStart v2 also supports a TanStack Router integration.

parallelRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

interceptedRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

prefetch.note: FileRoutes maps page files and dynamic segments; Solid Router supplies nested layout/navigation behavior. SolidStart v2 also supports a TanStack Router integration.

softNavigation.note: Solid Router's delegated link handling and navigation primitives update route content and browser history without a full reload. Explicit link/reload controls determine which anchors are intercepted.
softNavigation.label: Solid Router

viewTransitions.note: The reviewed routing API does not establish this navigation capability. Application code or another package may provide it; this finding is not proof of absence.

redirects.note: FileRoutes maps page files and dynamic segments; Solid Router supplies nested layout/navigation behavior. SolidStart v2 also supports a TanStack Router integration.

serverData.note: Solid Router query/createAsync loads cached data and preloads route reads; use server keeps the body on the server.
serverData.label: Solid Router queries

clientData.note: Solid Router query/createAsync loads cached data and preloads route reads; use server keeps the body on the server.
clientData.label: Solid Router queries

requestDedupe.note: Solid Router query/createAsync loads cached data and preloads route reads; use server keeps the body on the server.
requestDedupe.label: Solid Router queries

persistentCache.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

invalidation.note: Solid Router actions revalidate queries and expose submission state.
invalidation.label: Solid Router actions

isr.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

apiRoutes.note: Route files export HTTP method handlers returning Responses, with typed request/route context.

httpErrors.note: The v2 HttpStatusCode component sets the server response status, and Start’s default error boundary selects 500. Applications must set 404 for their catch-all/missing-record UI or return an explicit endpoint Response. Client-only fallback UI does not alter the original HTTP response; decide status before streaming headers are sent.
httpErrors.label: HttpStatusCode / server response

actions.note: The use server directive extracts server functions and provides a browser-callable transport; authorization is still checked inside protected functions.

forms.note: Router actions accept form data and expose pending/error state. Validation is authored in the action or supplied by a validation library.
forms.label: Solid Router actions

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Router actions accept form data and expose pending/error state. Validation is authored in the action or supplied by a validation library.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Configured H3 middleware wraps request handling and exposes request-scoped locals.

cookies.note: SolidStart exposes H3 cookie helpers and encrypted cookie-session operations; secrets and cookie flags require configuration.

cssModules.note: Vite integration supports module.css files and scoped imported class names, including SSR CSS deduplication.

scopedCss.note: Vite integration supports module.css files and scoped imported class names, including SSR CSS deduplication.

tailwind.note: The Vite styling workflow can import CSS generated by Tailwind, and the guide demonstrates a route stylesheet importing tailwindcss. Tailwind is an external compiler; this is separate from a CSS-in-JS integration.
tailwind.label: Tailwind / Vite

cssInJs.note: The reviewed v2 styling guide establishes CSS and CSS Modules, but does not establish a named CSS-in-JS integration with documented server-rendering behavior. General Vite compatibility is not sufficient evidence of that SSR contract.

images.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

fonts.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

scripts.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

assetPipeline.note: SolidStart’s Vite pipeline hashes imported assets and updates production URLs. The static-asset guide distinguishes these imports from public/ files, which keep their original names and require their own cache-busting strategy.
assetPipeline.label: Vite asset imports

staticAssets.note: Public files retain stable URLs; imported assets receive Vite-generated hashed filenames.

metadata.note: Solid Meta provides reactive Title, Meta and Link components under MetaProvider, including server collection and client navigation updates.
metadata.label: Solid Meta

dynamicMetadata.note: Solid Meta provides reactive Title, Meta and Link components under MetaProvider, including server collection and client navigation updates.
dynamicMetadata.label: Solid Meta

metadataInheritance.note: MetaProvider composes descendant head components. The reviewed guide does not establish a general nested object merge/reset contract for inherited SEO fields.
metadataInheritance.label: Component composition

metadataOverrides.note: MetaProvider composes descendant head components. The reviewed guide does not establish a general nested object merge/reset contract for inherited SEO fields.

translations.note: Solid Primitives supplies reactive dictionaries and translation helpers; application code supplies locale policy.

localeFormatting.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

auth.note: The guide implements application-owned session/user checks in queries and server functions. A bundled account/provider service is not established.
auth.label: Session recipe

csp.note: The guide shows app-authored nonce/CSP middleware and CSRF checks. These must be installed and configured; the recipe is not automatic global enforcement.
csp.label: Security middleware recipe

cspNonce.note: The official security guide supplies a middleware recipe for generating a random nonce and matching HTTP policy. createHandler's nonce option coordinates generated renderer scripts. Apps own middleware installation and policy coverage; v2's JSON serialization avoids unsafe-eval.
cspNonce.label: Configured createHandler nonce

csrf.note: The guide shows app-authored nonce/CSP middleware and CSRF checks. These must be installed and configured; the recipe is not automatic global enforcement.
csrf.label: Security middleware recipe

environment.note: Server functions can read private runtime session secrets. Keep those values in server-only code and out of returned props/results.

types.note: SolidStart's TypeScript/Vite setup supplies typed application APIs and development hot updates.

hmr.note: SolidStart's TypeScript/Vite setup supplies typed application APIs and development hot updates.

cli.note: The Solid scaffolding tool creates SolidStart templates; project scripts run Vite development and production builds.
cli.label: Create Solid

bundleAnalysis.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart tooling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

unitTests.note: The guide documents Vitest with Solid Testing Library and Playwright for browser workflows; these are external test tools.
unitTests.label: Vitest / Playwright

e2eTests.note: The guide documents Vitest with Solid Testing Library and Playwright for browser workflows; these are external test tools.
e2eTests.label: Vitest / Playwright

observability.note: Not established in the reviewed SolidStart testing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

errorHandling.note: Solid ErrorBoundary catches rendering and reactive-update errors in its subtree and provides a fallback/reset function. It does not catch arbitrary event-handler or unrelated asynchronous callback failures; HTTP status handling is a separate concern.
errorHandling.label: Solid ErrorBoundary

serverHosting.note: Vite deployment plugins such as Nitro, Cloudflare and Netlify determine runtime output. Target compatibility depends on the plugin and server dependencies.
serverHosting.label: Deployment plugins

subpathProxy.note: The reviewed v2 source derives the server mount from Vite’s path base or explicit server.baseURL and uses it for server-function URLs. Router links and deployment-plugin public-origin handling must also match. An external CDN asset base is deliberately separate from the application mount; a complete proxy deployment still requires coordinated setup.
subpathProxy.label: Vite/server base; adapter setup

jobs.note: Nitro tasks can run or be scheduled outside request handling. The documented task runner is not a durable queue with retries/acknowledgement.
jobs.label: Nitro tasks

realtime.note: The documented Nitro v3 plugin enables cross-platform WebSocket handlers. Applications own authorization and pub/sub topology.
realtime.label: Nitro WebSockets

xssEscaping.note: Its integrated UI renderer supplies this policy. JSX text interpolation uses text output; innerHTML is a raw-HTML sink. Applications must sanitize untrusted content supplied to innerHTML.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: Server-backed Solid Router actions can be used as real HTML form actions, so the server handles submissions before JavaScript loads. Keep the use-server handler and native form action; an action implemented only as browser fetch is not a no-JavaScript endpoint.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Server-backed Router actions

optimisticUi.note: Solid resource mutation/submission APIs let the application display optimistic data, but confirmation, rollback and overlapping mutations need application logic.
